entry.title: Copilot Spaces in the IDE
entry.content:
Value Prop

We are bringing Copilot Spaces to the IDEs: VSCode, Jetbrains, and Visual Studio.

Automate Repetitive Tasks
All software companies have routine tasks required as part of development. For example, at GitHub, we often need to add new telemetry, create new services, write test cases, or add a feature flag wrapper before we can release a new feature. These are simple tasks, but they are performed often enough to introduce toil. Sometimes, they must be done across multiple repos. Spaces can be used as a container for relevant information (such as code samples, instructions, documentation, and more), and then scaffold out the changes using Agent mode.

Review Local Changes
Many customers have specific policies related to code development such as accessibility standards, security standards, or code quality standards. Often, these are documented in a central repository as markdown. Sometimes, they are hosted on another platform like Notion or Google Drive. Spaces can be used for comparing local changes against documented standards in order to ensure compliance.

Facilitate Migrations
Library or framework upgrades can be a major challenge in some codebases. You can set up Spaces which contain documentation on the old and new frameworks, example code for both the before and after, and acceptance criteria as custom instructions.

Expected Outcome

Developers can chat with a Copilot Space or use it with agent mode in the IDE.

entry.title: Copilot Spaces [GA]
entry.content:
Value Prop

Context is messy. Code "systems" are often abstractly defined. Documentation is often scattered, nonexistent, or outdated. This means that it can be difficult for AI agents to search and incorporate the right context autonomously.

Thankfully, in every company or codebase, someone knows where the “__” logic is defined. So as long as you can make it fast and easy for developers to set the context that they want to use and even share that with teammates, then you’ll have better quality responses.

Expected Outcome

The GA of Copilot Spaces brings the feature to all developers on github.

entry.title: Native integration of GitHub Artifact Attestations with JFrog Evidence for policy-driven governance
entry.content:
Value Prop

With increasing emphasis on software supply chain security and compliance, organizations need reliable ways to ensure only trusted artifacts are promoted and released. This integration enables organizations to use GitHub-generated artifact attestations, including provenance, SBOMs, and custom attestations, as signed, verifiable evidence within JFrog’s Evidence Collection. By supporting native ingestion of GitHub attestations, customers can automatically gate the promotion of artifacts in Artifactory based on the presence and validity of attestations created by trusted GitHub workflows.

Expected Outcome

With the integration enabled, attestations generated on GitHub are automatically ingested into JFrog Evidence Collection. These attestations can then be used to enforce policies that govern artifact promotion, release readiness, and compliance requirements. For example, organizations can require that only artifacts with valid, GitHub-signed attestations are eligible for promotion or deployment, ensuring that every release meets internal and regulatory standards before reaching production.

entry.title: Production-Aware Dependabot Alerts (in partnership with JFrog Artifactory)
entry.content:
Value Prop

Customers using JFrog Artifactory alongside GitHub’s security products have often struggled to connect vulnerability alerts in source code with the true risks facing their production environments. With our new integration, JFrog Artifactory will automatically send authoritative artifact metadata to GitHub, enabling Dependabot to surface and prioritize only those alerts that impact artifacts actually stored in your production-approved package repositories. This integration reduces alert fatigue and ensures security teams spend their time remediating vulnerabilities that represent real, actionable risk to production systems, improving both focus and efficiency.

Expected Outcome

With this integration, teams will gain end-to-end traceability across their software supply chain, from code to production. Dependabot alerts will become more targeted and relevant, highlighting only vulnerabilities that could affect software deployed from your approved Artifactory repositories. Security and engineering teams will benefit from streamlined workflows, faster remediation, and greater confidence that their efforts are protecting their critical systems.

entry.title: Copilot Now Supports Configuring Remote 3P MCP Servers
entry.content:
Value Prop

GitHub Copilot now allows users to easily install remote third-party Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers. This empowers developers to easily connect Copilot with external sources outside the GitHub ecosystem, making it possible to bring in critical context into your conversations with Copilot.

Expected Outcome

By supporting remote MCP servers, Copilot becomes significantly more knowledgeable and useful.

entry.title: Copilot Issue Creation Now Supports Issue Forms
entry.content:
Value Prop

GitHub Copilot issue creation just got more powerful. It now supports issue forms, ensuring that issues created with Copilot are high-quality, complete, and structured according to each repository's standards. It also supports breaking down epics into sub-issues, saving you valuable time on how to best structure and sequence your work.

Expected Outcome

With Copilot supporting issue forms and sub issues, users can expect faster, high quality issue creation.

entry.title: Dependencies on Issues [Preview]
entry.content:
Value Prop

Teams can now define dependencies between issues, making it easy to identify what needs to be done before other work can start. This brings new levels of clarity and coordination to projects, especially those managing complex workflows.

Expected Outcome

Customers will be able to mark dependencies between issues, enabling better planning, prioritization, and execution of work. This improvement helps teams avoid blockers, improve delivery timelines, and confidently manage project progress directly within GitHub.

entry.title: Copilot Chat users can use the Gemini 2.5 Flash model
entry.content:
Value Prop

GitHub Copilot now offers multi-model support, allowing developers to choose from industry-leading models, including Google's Gemini 2.5 Flash, to power their coding assistance. This flexibility enables developers to select the most suitable model for their specific use case, ensuring optimal performance and efficiency. By integrating multiple models into familiar workflows in Visual Studio Code and on github.com/copilot, GitHub is enhancing the developer experience and providing tailored AI-powered solutions.

Expected Outcome

By leveraging GitHub Copilot's multi-model support, developers can expect increased productivity and improved code quality by selecting the best model for each task. This feature empowers developers to handle diverse programming challenges more effectively, resulting in faster development cycles and more robust software solutions. Additionally, the seamless integration of Google's Gemini 2.5 Flash ensures that developers have access to advanced AI capabilities, enhancing their ability to tackle complex coding problems from concept to deployment.

entry.title: Org-owned Apps can be managed using Teams and the org roles system [Preview]
entry.content:
Value Prop

You can now use the Organization Roles system to assign the App Manager role to users and teams in your organization, allowing them to manage all GitHub Apps in your organization. Previously this was a bespoke system specific to Apps, and was not integrated into the roles platform. This means you can now use the Organization Role APIs to assign the App Manager role to users and teams as well.

In addition, you can now assign teams to specific GitHub Apps, instead of just assigning users. While this cannot be done programmatically, you will be able to programmatically (or via SCIM or team sync) manage the members of the team, who are now allowed to manage the GitHub App.

Expected Outcome

More resilient app management patterns, with greater flexibility and scalability for the assignment of the app manager role. This also sets the foundation for the future, where you'll be able to create custom roles such as "View all apps" or "Can create apps" using the new app management permissions, letting your organization members get more access to apps in a safe manner.

entry.title: Enterprise-owned Apps can be managed individually by users [Preview]
entry.content:
Value Prop

You can now add enterprise members as managers of a GitHub App owned by your enterprise.

App managers have full privileges over the application, with one exception: if they modify application permissions, those changes are not automatically accepted by organizations where the app is installed. App managers do not have sufficient privileges to force permission updates onto organizations. Only enterprise admins can update application permissions without requiring approval from each organization.

Expected Outcome

This lets the Enterprise Admin focus their time on managing the enterprise and less time updating applications for their members. In the future, we'll also have enterprise-wide roles for app management, as well as support for enterprise teams.

entry.title: Support VSS bundles for metered GHE
entry.content:
Value Prop

Introducing metered GitHub Enterprise billing for Visual Studio subscriptions with GitHub Enterprise.

Scaling your GitHub usage is even easier. GitHub is expanding our pay-as-you-go usage-based billing and licensing reporting interface to include GitHub Enterprise (GHE) for Visual Studio subscriptions with GitHub Enterprise usage.

Expected Outcome

We announced pay-as-you-go billing for GHE and GHAS back in August 1, 2024 to give customers flexible self-provisioning and pricing. Since then, we've heard increasing demand to also have the same billing mechanism for accounts using Visual Studio subscriptions with GitHub Enterprise. Now, you not only have greater flexibility with pay-as-you-go billing, but administrators will also have greater control in mapping which users should consume a Visual Studio license versus a GitHub Enterprise metered license.

entry.title: Enhanced Repository Creation [Preview]
entry.content:
Value Prop

The new repository creation form is a streamlined, custom properties-forward experience that enables organizations to create compliant repositories by default. It allows administrators to link custom properties and policies at the point of creation while providing developers with a more intuitive, modern interface that surfaces relevant options.

Repository creation with required properties

Repository creation without required properties

Expected Outcome

With the new repository creation form you will experience a streamlined, intuitive creation flow that reduces friction while surfacing the right options. Administrators can have confidence that all new repositories meet organizational standards without manual oversight, eliminating the need for approval processes and enabling "secure by default" repository creation at scale.

entry.title: Immutable Releases [GA]
entry.content:
Value Prop

Immutable Releases introduces enhanced integrity and security for software distributed via GitHub Releases. With this feature, repository maintainers can publish releases and associated assets as immutable, ensuring that once a release is published, its assets and associated Git tag cannot be altered or deleted. This prevents supply chain attacks that rely on asset modification or tag movement after publication, and provides users with stronger guarantees that the artifacts they consume are exactly as originally published. Immutable Releases also introduces release attestations, allowing consumers to verify the origin and integrity of artifacts—even outside of GitHub.

Expected Outcome

  • Organizations and open-source projects can confidently distribute software through GitHub Releases, knowing assets and tags cannot be tampered with after publication.
  • Consumers and downstream automation will be able to reliably verify that downloaded artifacts are authentic and unmodified, reducing risk in the software supply chain.
  • The introduction of release attestations provides verifiable proof of artifact origin and content, supporting secure end-to-end software delivery.
  • Immutable Releases aligns GitHub Releases with best practices for provenance and immutability, supporting compliance, security, and trust for all users.

entry.title: Expose Release Asset Digests [GA]
entry.content:
Value Prop

GitHub will now automatically compute and display checksums (SHA256 digests) for all uploaded release assets, making these digests available both in the UI and via the API. The checksums are generated at the time of asset upload and are immutable, providing a consistent and standardized way for all projects on GitHub to offer checksum data for their releases.

Expected Outcome

Users and automation tools can easily verify that the asset they downloaded hasn't been tampered with after publishing.

entry.title: Make billing usage reports more useful by providing a summarized report option
entry.content:
Value Prop

Customers depend on the billing usage report to analyze their usage-based charges and build confidence in GitHub’s billing platform. We frequently hear from our customers that the current report is too dense, resulting in files that are too large to work with effectively. By introducing a summarized usage report, we aim to cover the majority of customer use cases in a more accessible format. For those who need full detail, the detailed report will remain available and its underlying query will also be optimized as part of this release.

Expected Outcome

With summarized billing usage reports, customers will be able to self-serve and better understand their GitHub usage. Customers who previously encountered issues—such as reports not generating or being too large to analyze—will now be able to access the insights they expect when requesting billing data.

entry.title: Copilot Vision integration in Copilot Chat on GitHub Mobile
entry.content:
Value Prop

This feature allows users to transform mermaid diagrams and process images on the go with Copilot Vision, leveraging mobile-native capabilities for enhanced productivity.

Expected Outcome

Users can improve their workflows by seamlessly generating and interacting with visual content directly from their mobile devices, reducing reliance on desktop tools.

entry.title: OPA Gatekeeper support for Artifact Attestations
entry.content:
Value Prop

This release introduces a plugin for OPA Gatekeeper, enabling the verification of Artifact Attestations. Integrated with major cloud providers, Gatekeeper acts as a Kubernetes admission controller, allowing enforcement of attestation verification to gate deployments. This ensures that only trusted and verified artifacts are deployed, enhancing end-to-end SDLC security.

Expected Outcome

Organizations using OPA Gatekeeper as their Kubernetes admission controller will be able to enforce attestation verification, enhancing end-to-end build security.

entry.title: Insights for Copilot adoption, engagement and impact [Preview]
entry.content:
Value Prop

Our dashboards for Copilot engagement and impact will provide organizations with insights at the organizational level to maximize the value of Copilot. These dashboards offer data related to onboarding Copilot users, understanding engagement with specific Copilot features, and assessing early indicators of Copilot's impact on the engineering system. By delivering actionable metrics, these dashboards enable organizations to optimize their use of Copilot, enhance productivity, and drive AI-driven innovation.

Expected Outcome

Organizations can expect improved visibility into the adoption and engagement of Copilot, and actionable insights to refine deployment and maximize Copilot's value. Bring a data-driven approach to your deployment and optimization of Copilot. The images below are subject to change.

entry.title: Security Configurations include "Default or Advanced Setup" option for Code Scanning [GA]
entry.content:
Value Prop

Our new "Default or Advanced" option gives security managers the freedom to choose the setup that best fits their organization, while ensuring security requirements are consistently met across their repositories. This will allow enforcement of security configurations to hold even when some repositories need to use Advanced Setup for code scanning, solving a common customer pain point with security configurations and code scanning.

Expected Outcome

This will result in more repositories with code scanning running properly and fewer repositories that need bespoke security configurations.
